records.text:
About MoleculeOS
About MoleculeOS
MoleculeOS is an operating system for life science R&D in the programmable biology era (AI-native Bio-OS). It bridges the understanding and design of biomolecules (proteins), interprets scientific intent within real R&D contexts, and centrally orchestrates pipelines to drive research workflows.

records.title: Preface
records.text:
Preface
Preface
What can MoleculeOS do for you?


Without writing scripts, you can issue tasks directly in natural language via the chat interface:

Molecular Computing & Intelligent Design

-   Structure Prediction: Input sequences to automatically predict 3D structures of proteins, antibodies, or complexes, assess regional confidence metrics, and generate multiple models for evaluation.
-   Mutation Effect Prediction: Run four complementary scoring dimensions in a single step—sequence fitness, evolutionary conservation, structural folding stability, and binding affinity. Cross-filter robust variants across multiple parameters to prevent single-metric bias.
-   Antibody Humanization (Beta): Input antibody sequences to automatically execute the humanization pipeline and output ranked candidate sequences that retain antigen-binding capability.
-   Homology Search & 3D Visualization: Identify distant homolog proteins and analyze evolutionary relationships. Highlight specific residues, measure distances, and customize display representations in the 3D molecular viewer for clear structural insights.

Expert Antibody Engineering Workflows

-   Binding Mode Analysis: Intelligently identify heavy chains, light chains, and antigens within complex structures. Perform deep-dive analyses of interface interactions (hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, hydrophobic contacts, π-π stacking, etc.) and generate structured reports with biological interpretations.
-   Affinity Optimization & Developability Assessment: Score sequences across sequence, structure, evolution, and binding free energy in parallel to locate high-potential mutation sites. Automatically scan CDR regions for liability motifs (e.g., glycosylation, deamidation, oxidation) to mitigate downstream process and stability risks early.

Rational Enzyme Engineering

-   Catalytic Mechanism & Activity Optimization: Identify active-site residues and analyze catalytic triads or cofactor-binding modes. Recommend substitution strategies to enhance catalytic efficiency based on pocket geometry and sequence conservation.
-   Stability Enhancement & Conformational Analysis: Differentiate active-site residues from scaffold positions to propose precise thermostability mutations (e.g., disulfide engineering, hydrophobic core optimization) without impairing catalytic function. Compare substrate-bound and apo states to track critical loop dynamics.

Target Research & Construct Design

-   Target Landscape Research: Input target names or gene symbols to automatically aggregate UniProt annotations, PDB structures, and literature into a comprehensive report.
-   Expression Construct Design: Identify topological features such as signal peptides, transmembrane regions, and domain boundaries to recommend optimal expression fragments, affinity tags, and host systems for structural or functional assays.


How Does It Work?


MoleculeOS is more than a simple computation portal—it operates as an AI collaborator equipped with scientific reasoning:

-   Research First, Compute Second: Before running heavy computations, the system analyzes biological context using literature and curated databases to avoid unstructured calculation runs.
-   Autonomous Planning & Parallel Execution: Complex objectives are decomposed into structured workflows. Long-running computational tasks execute in the background via multithreading without blocking ongoing user interaction.
-   Cross-Validation & Transparent Reporting: Results are cross-referenced with established biological principles and flagged if discrepancies arise. Missing data or assumption-based inferences are explicitly documented.


Target Audience


-   Wet-Lab Scientists (Antibody, Protein, and Enzyme Engineers): Gain structure-based rational design suggestions and multi-dimensional scoring support for humanization, affinity maturation, thermostability optimization, or catalytic mechanism studies.
-   Dry-Lab Specialists (Computational Biologists & Protein Designers): Automate repetitive scripting and data-wrangling pipelines, delegating workflow execution to focus on higher-level scientific evaluation.

records.text:
1.1 Registration and Login
1. Quick Start
New User Registration


URL: https://mos.moleculemind.com/


Individual Users


The platform supports open registration for individual accounts using a valid email address.

Step 1: Enter your email address and accept the User Agreement and Privacy Policy.



  

Step 2: Enter the verification code received via email and click Next.



Step 3: Set your password and complete your profile information.



Step 4: Account creation complete.

Click Get Started to access the platform.




Enterprise Access Requests


Advanced permissions are available for enterprise organizations. To request enterprise onboarding, send an inquiry to [mos@moleculemind.com](mailto:mos@moleculemind.com). Access tiers will be provisioned following verification.




Login


-   Individual Users: Log in using your registered username/email and password.
-   Enterprise Users: Log in using the enterprise identifier, username, and password assigned by your administrator.










Password Recovery


If you forget your password, click "Forgot password?" on the login page and follow the guided verification steps to reset your credentials.

records.title: 1.2 MoleculeOS Main Interface
records.text:
1.2 MoleculeOS Main Interface
1. Quick Start
Top Navigation Bar: Houses project switching, sharing options, system notifications, and account settings.

Left Node Tree:

-   Protein Nodes: Displays all protein structures loaded in the active project. Click any node to select and switch focus.
-   Amino Acid Groups: Displays user-defined residue annotations and selection groups.

Central Display Area: Shows sequence attributes (top panel) and 3D molecular structures (bottom panel) for the currently selected protein.

Basic Toolbar: Contains standard viewing operations, including Zoom In/Out, Center/Reset, Representation controls, Distance measurement, Overlay toggling, and Interaction views.

Floating Toolbar: Houses core execution modules, including Superimposition, Model Execution, Homology Search, and the Mocha AI Assistant.

records.title: 2.1 Project Management
records.text:
2.1 Project Management
2. Core Platform Features
Project Concept


Projects in MoleculeOS serve as dedicated workspaces for specific protein engineering campaigns. Users can organize, track, and share all associated proteins, computational tasks, and analysis pipelines within a single secure environment.


Viewing the Project List


Click the dropdown menu next to the current project name in the top navigation bar to view all accessible projects.






Creating a Project


Open the project list, click "Create Project", provide a project title and description, and click "Submit". The creator is designated as the Project Owner.




Switching Projects


Open the project dropdown menu and click on the target project name to switch workspaces.




Editing Project Metadata


Project Owners and Editors have permission to modify project settings. Hover over a project entry in the list, click the edit icon, update the name or description, and click "Submit" to save changes.




Deleting a Project


Project Owners and Editors can delete non-default projects. Hover over the target project in the list, click the delete icon, and confirm the prompt.




Project Sharing


Project Owners and Project Editors have the permission to share projects via:

-   Option 1 - Copy Link: Click "Share" in the top navigation bar, select "Share link", and copy the URL.
-   Option 2 - Member Invitations: Add team members directly by user handle or email.



Grant specific users access to this project by adding project members. For detailed operation steps, please refer to the section below.


Project Member Management


-   Adding Members: Click Share, search for colleagues within your organization, assign their permission level (Read or Edit), and click Invite.



-   Removing Members: Open the member list in the Share panel and click the remove icon next to the relevant user.



-   Modifying Permissions: Adjust access levels directly using the permission dropdown selector next to each member's name.

records.title: 2.5 Basic Toolbar
records.text:
2.5 Basic Toolbar
2. Core Platform Features
Located on the right side of the Structure View, this toolbar provides essential inspection utilities: zoom, reset, representation modes, non-covalent interactions, and more.


Zoom in/Zoom out


Adjust scale using the mouse scroll wheel or click the Zoom In / Zoom Out buttons on the toolbar to scale the structure relative to the viewport center.




Reset


After panning, rotating, or zooming, click "Reset" to return the structure to its default center and orientation.




Representation Styles


Switching representations aids in examining secondary structures, binding pockets, and interface contacts.

MoleculeOS provides three standard representations:












Method 1: Global Representation Change


-   Target Selection: In the left protein tree, expand the protein node and select the target chain or model.
-   Invoke function: Hover over the icon next to the node to reveal the options menu.
-   Select Style: Choose from Cartoon, Ball and Stick, or Surface to apply the rendering style globally.




Method 2: Local Representation Change


-   Target Selection: Select specific residues in the structure or sequence view (multi-selection supported).
-   Select Style: Click the desired style button on the right toolbar to update only the selected residues.




Residue Distance Measurement


MoleculeOS supports the measurement of the distance between two residues, which is measured in Å with a precision of two decimal places.

-   Select Residues: Select two target residues in the structure or sequence viewer.
-   Execute: Click the Distance tool on the toolbar to display the calculated measurement.




Overlay Visibility Toggle (Invisible / Visible)


Temporarily hide labels, measurements, and overlay data to declutter the viewport.

Click the visibility icon on the toolbar to toggle all overlay annotations on or off.

records.title: 2.6 Floating toolbar
records.text:
2.6 Floating toolbar 
2. Core Platform Features
Positioned at the bottom of the screen, the floating toolbar houses core analytical capabilities: structural superimposition, model execution, homology search, and Mocha AI.


Structural Superimposition


Aligns multiple protein structures to compare structural variations and binding site conformations.

-   Select & Launch: Select the candidate proteins in the left node tree, then click "Superimpose" on the bottom toolbar.



-   Select Proteins: Check two or more structures in the selection modal.
-   Select Reference Structure:
-   "Fixed" designates the static reference structure against which all other structures align. Click the "Fixed" tag to toggle it to "Moving", and vice versa.
-   Click the "Fixed" tag to switch it to "Moving". Click "Moving" to switch it back to "Fixed".
-   A group can only have one reference protein; all other proteins are automatically set to "Moving".
-   Select chains to align: Because a protein may contain multiple chains, choose which chain to use for alignment across all proteins.



-   Confirm: Click "Confirm" to align the selected proteins.





Note: If you only see one protein in the viewer after completing these steps, make sure you selected the corresponding proteins in the left node tree first.

The operation example is shown in the following figure


















Residue Annotation


When you find valuable positions through papers, databases, or filtering, use "Annotation" to save them in your project. Anyone with project access can view these annotations.

Only project Owners and Editors can create, edit, and delete annotations. Viewers can only view them.

-   Select target residues: Select one or multiple residues directly in the structure or sequence view.



-   Open the tool: Click "Annotation" on the bottom toolbar.



-   Review and adjust residue format:
-   View selected residues: The panel displays all currently selected residues.
-   Advanced settings: The default format is "3-letter+Position". You can switch to "1-letter+Position" or click "Advanced" to adjust the display to your preference.



-   Name the group and confirm: Enter a name and description for the residue group, then click "Confirm". The group will appear under "Amino acid group" in the left panel.



-   Accessing annotations later:
-   Quick locate: Hover over an "AA Group" node to highlight the corresponding positions in both the sequence and structure views simultaneously.
-   Open and Copy: Hovering over an "AA Group" node reveals two actions:
-   Click "Open" to view the annotation details again.
-   Click "Copy" to copy the residue information to your clipboard.









-   Delete a node (Owner and Editor only):
-   Open the annotation details and click the "More" button in the top right.
-   Select delete and confirm to remove the node.


Residue Search (5Å)


After selecting one or more residues, you can filter for surrounding residues based on distance and type. Use this feature to save key sites to your project so other members can view them.

Only project Owners and Editors can create, edit, and delete. Viewers can only view.

-   Select residues: Select one or multiple target residues in the structure or sequence view.



-   Open the tool: Click "5Å" on the bottom toolbar.



-   Set filter criteria (the tool takes the intersection of both conditions):
-   Distance: Filters residues within a defined radius around the selected amino acids. Supports a range of 1 Å to 10 Å with 0.1 Å precision. Use the up/down arrows for 0.5 Å increments, or type a value directly.
-   Residue Type: Select specific amino acid types to narrow down the selection.
-   Name and confirm: Once filtered, click "Next", enter a name and description, and click "Confirm". The group will be saved under "Amino acid group" on the left.
-   View / Copy / Delete: Follow the same steps as Annotation.

4. Homologous Protein Search (SeqSimSearch)
During protein design and optimization, homologous proteins provide valuable reference data, such as conserved sites and functional characteristics. MoleculeOS connects directly to external databases. Once you input a target sequence or chain and set filtering parameters, it returns a ranked list of homologs based on similarity.


Search by target sequence


On the bottom toolbar, click "SeqSim Search". In the panel, select "Search by Sequence", enter the query sequence, and click "Search" to create a task. You will be notified once it completes.




Search by target chain


In the panel, select "Search by My Protein", choose the target protein and its chain, and click "Blast" to create a task. You will be notified once it completes.




View results


When the task finishes, open the notification in the top navigation bar and click "Visualizing Data" to load the results into your project.

The homolog list will open on the right panel. The list displays: Protein ID (from PDB, UniProt, or NCBI), Hit and match score, E-value, Bit score, %ID, and Reference.



Expand any row to view the pairwise sequence alignment between the query and the hit.




Set filter criteria


When there are too many results, use the "Filter" tool to narrow them down.



Click "Reset" and confirm to clear filters.




Download data


MoleculeOS supports exporting homolog data locally in FASTA format:

-   Download all

Exports all protein sequences in the list.



-   Download selected

Check the target proteins and use the download icon in the upper right.



-   Download single hit

Directly download an individual hit entry.




Visit source database


Click the "Reference" hyperlink on any entry to open the corresponding source database page.




Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA)


Select multiple proteins from the list and click "Align" below to run a multiple sequence alignment.




Metric Definitions


-   ID: Identifier of the matched sequence.
-   Hit: Subject sequence in the database (specified under Reference).
-   Score: Raw alignment score calculated from matches, mismatches, and gap penalties; used to compare results within the same search.
-   E-value: Expect value representing the number of chance alignments expected in the database (e.g., an E-value of 1 indicates a likely random match, whereas 1e-50 indicates high confidence).
-   Bit score: Normalized score derived from the raw score; allows comparison across different searches.
-   % ID: Percentage of identical amino acids across the aligned region, including gaps.
-   Reference: Source database containing the hit sequence.

Starting a Conversation


Projects open in "agent mode on" by default. Mocha is an AI assistant in MoleculeOS that executes tasks by calling appropriate models based on your requests in the chat interface below.

Start a Mocha conversation: enter a research goal in the project chat and submit the request.

For example, in an antibody design task, Mocha can propose affinity-enhancing mutations based on input antibody and antigen sequences.

You can test Mocha's antibody optimization workflow with the following sample input:

Prompt: Please predict the structure from the given input sequence, and recommend a list of 30 mutations that may improve antibody affinity while avoiding positions that already interact with the antigen.



Python

>antigen



>heavy chain

>light chain

ALVMTQTPSSVSAAVGGTVTINCQASQNIYSGLAWYQQKLGQPPKLLIYKASTLASGVPSRFKGSGSGTQFTLTISGVQCDDAATYYCQLAYSSTNVDNAFGGGTEVVVK



The complete process of using Mocha to run this task is shown in the following video:

Full Mocha workflow example: from a research request to analysis results.


Task Decomposition


Based on your prompt, Mocha breaks the task into sequential steps and identifies the required model for each step.




Task


Click the "Task" button in the upper right to view the task list, execution status, and runtimes.

Click an individual task to view its detailed execution log.

Review Task: open the task list and check computation status.


Result Output


Once all tasks are complete, Mocha outputs an analysis report that typically includes:

-   Structure prediction: Displays molecular composition, sequence length, predicted structure, and quality metrics.
-   Structure and functional analysis: Details key regions, binding interfaces, interactions, and critical residues.
-   Candidate mutation recommendations: Lists suggested mutations, positions, scores, and rationales.
-   Summary: Summarizes key findings and provides recommendations for downstream screening or validation.

Review Mocha results: read the completed analysis and inspect output files.

records.text:
6. MMetrics
6. MMetrics
MMetrics provides high-value protein data to help users understand and analyze protein structures.


Triggering MMetrics


When a protein is loaded into a project, MMetrics automatically starts calculations. Proteins can originate from:

-   Local uploads (supports .pdb and .cif formats)
-   Structures generated via MoleculeOS calculations (such as MMFold or DeNovo)
-   Structures loaded into the project via PDB ID

Currently supported protein types:

-   Enzyme + small molecule complexes
-   Antibody + antigen complexes


Description


MMetrics starts with an overview summarizing basic information to give you a quick profile of the protein, including:

-   Protein type and classification confidence
-   Protein name, source, function, and key structural features
-   Basis for the classification
-   Chains and their respective molecule types




Homologous Proteins


MMetrics searches for homologous proteins and displays the top five results ranked by match confidence. Information for each homolog includes:

-   PDB ID
-   Crystal structure label (if applicable)
-   Sequence identity (% ID)
-   Reference link (clickable for direct navigation)

Review homologs: inspect matches, sequence identity, and Reference links.


Annotations


"Annotations" displays residues and regions with specific functional roles:

-   For enzymes, it annotates the binding pocket and active site.
-   For antibodies, it annotates epitope data, CDR regions, and light/heavy chains.

Clicking a region name highlights the corresponding area in the 3D structure viewer on the left. Multiple regions can be selected at once; click "clear" to reset all active selections.

Region annotations: select a functional region to highlight it in 3D; use Clear to remove the selection.

Clicking a single residue highlights only that specific position in the 3D viewer.

Single-residue annotations: select a residue to locate its position in the structure.

For antibody-antigen complexes, you can select from four antibody numbering schemes: IMGT, Kabat, EU, and AHo.

Antibody numbering: switch numbering schemes and review CDR and chain annotations.


Interaction network


MMetrics can display interactions in either a table or a 2D diagram. Click "Table" or "2D" on the right to switch views.

Interaction network: switch between Table and 2D views.


Enzyme + Small Molecule:


In the 2D view, the small molecule is placed at the center, surrounded by interacting residues with their chain IDs and positions.

Dashed lines of different colors represent different interaction types.

Amino acid node colors indicate chemical properties (such as aromatic, sulfur-containing, or basic residues).

Click an interaction dashed line to display the distance between the small molecule and the protein.

Small-molecule 2D interactions: select an edge to inspect interaction type and distance.

An amino acid may have multiple interactions with the small molecule; click the residue directly to view all of its associated interactions.

Small-molecule residue interactions: select an amino acid to inspect its contacts.

Table View:

The Table view lists specific interactions between the ligand and surrounding residues:

-   Type: Interaction type
-   Ligand atom: Atom number of the interacting ligand atom
-   Residue: Residue interacting with the ligand
-   Dist (Å): Interaction distance between the ligand atom and residue in Angstroms (Å)
-   Top tags: Display the count of each interaction type



This view makes it easy to locate specific interacting atoms and residues and inspect their interaction types and distances.

Clicking an interaction row highlights the pair in the 3D viewer.

Interaction table: select a row to locate the atoms and residues in 3D.


Antibody + Antigen:


For antibody-antigen complexes, the 2D view displays interactions between individual antibody and antigen chains.

Dashed lines represent interaction types, node colors represent amino acid classes (see legend), and labels along the lines indicate interaction distances in Angstroms (Å).

Antibody–antigen 2D interactions: inspect interface residues and contact distances.

The Table view lists interaction types, antibody residues, antigen residues, and distances row by row.

Residues are shown in the format "Chain ID: Residue Name and Position" (for example, "H:TYR58" represents tyrosine at position 58 on the heavy chain).

Clicking an interaction row in the table highlights the corresponding sites in the 3D viewer.

Antibody–antigen interaction table: check chains, residues, interaction types, and distances.


Mutation Scoring


Mutation Scoring provides multi-dimensional evaluations across three CSV output files to assist with candidate screening:

-   MutXseq.csv: Evaluates mutations based on sequence-level features.
-   MutXstruct.csv: Evaluates mutations based on 3D structure and the local microenvironment.
-   MutXevo.csv: Evaluates mutations based on evolutionary conservation and homologous sequence alignments.

Each record includes:

-   Chain: Protein chain containing the mutation
-   Mutation: Specific substitution
-   Score: Calculated score for the mutation in that dimension

Click "View" to preview results online, or click "Download" to export the full CSV file. You can combine scores across all three dimensions for a comprehensive evaluation when selecting mutations.

Mutation scoring: use View to preview and Download to export CSV results.

records.text:
Function Introduction 
7. Model Catalog and Protein Computation (Function Call)
1. MMFold



Overview




MMFold is an advanced deep learning model that accurately predicts 3D protein structures using Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) as key inputs. By leveraging evolutionary information to identify structural motifs and residue interactions, it significantly enhances research efficiency in computational biology and structural bioinformatics.

Target Users

Biological Researchers: To assist experimental design and complement experimental observations with predicted structural data.

Use Cases

Protein Structure Prediction: Predict 3D structures from amino acid sequences to help elucidate function and biological mechanisms.

Cross-Species Structural Comparison: Compare predicted structures across different species to study evolutionary relationships and analyze structural conservation among homologs.

Industrial Enzyme Design: Provide structural insights to guide mutation design and optimize catalytic activity for biomanufacturing or pharmaceutical development.

Input

Input file (required): FASTA file containing protein sequences (different chains on the same line separated by a colon :).

Outputs

3D protein structure in PDB format.




Steps


-   Launch the model calculation and complete the required inputs as prompted.



-   View results: Open the task results panel and import the models into the MoleculeOS project. This tool generates three candidate PDB structures.




2. Protein Redesign



Overview




Redesigns amino acid sequences based on fixed protein backbone structures.

Target Users

Synthetic Biologists: Design and optimize the stability and catalytic activity of substrate-specific enzymes.

Drug Discovery Researchers: Design protein therapeutics such as antibodies.

Use Cases

Redesign full sequences based on a target protein structure.

Keep specific sequence regions fixed while redesigning the remaining positions.

Optimize and design sequences for enzymes targeting specific substrates.

Design binder sequences based on protein structures bound to therapeutic targets.

Design biosensors.

Inputs

Input File (Required): Protein structure file in CIF or PDB format (can contain multiple chains and small molecules).

Design Residues (Optional): Specific residues to redesign (e.g., "A1 A4 B2 B3").

Outputs

Protein sequences: redesign.fasta




Steps


1. Import a PDB/CIF structure, choose Protein Redesign in Mocha, and select the input structure. For a partial redesign, specify the design residues (for example A1 A4 B2 B3) and check the chain IDs and residue numbering before submitting.
2. Wait for Succeed in Task, then open the results panel to inspect redesign.fasta. Keep the input structure and task record for sequence comparisons.

7.2 · Input and submission

7.2 · Result review


3. Protein Binder Design



Overview




Designs target-specific binder proteins (backbone structures alone or including sequence).

Target Users

Synthetic Biologists: Design enzyme inhibitors or stabilizers.

Drug Discovery Researchers: Design mini-protein therapeutics, masking peptides, etc.

Use Cases

Inhibit enzyme activity by binding to active or allosteric sites.

Stabilize protein folding or prevent aggregation during expression.

Target disease-associated proteins as antibody alternatives (e.g., viral or oncology targets).

Deliver drugs or nanoparticles to specific tissues via targeted binding.

Mimic or block natural ligands to modulate receptor signaling pathways.

Target immune receptors to regulate immune responses.

Inputs

"Input Structure" (Required): File containing the target protein structure (can contain multiple chains).

"Target Binding" (Required): Target protein residues in the intended binding region (e.g., "A5 A8-20" specifies residue 5 and residues 8 through 20 on Chain A).

"Binder Size Min" (Required): Minimum length of the designed binder peptide (e.g., 15).

"Binder Size Max" (Required): Maximum length of the designed binder peptide (e.g., 30).

"Align Binder" (Optional): When enabled, MoleculeOS predicts the target-binder complex and aligns it against the original target chain.

Outputs

Designed binder structure containing heavy-atom 3D coordinates and virtual amino acid annotations: output.cif

If mosapp_compare_binder==1, the complex structure of the target protein and binder peptide containing valid sequences: aligned.cif




Steps


1. Import the target structure and choose Protein Binder Design in Mocha. Specify Target Binding residues and Binder Size Min / Max. Enable Align Binder when complex prediction and alignment are needed.
2. Check the task status in Task. After success, open output.cif and, when alignment is enabled, inspect aligned.cif. Import the results to review the target and candidate binder geometry.

7.3 · Input and submission

7.3 · Candidate outputs


4. Sequence Fitness Mutation Effect



Overview




Predicts protein structure, function, and evolutionary relationships to comprehensively evaluate all potential and viable single-point mutations across a protein sequence.

Target Users

Protein Engineers: Design and optimize protein or enzyme functions.

Drug Developers: Assess the impact of mutations on therapeutic target proteins.

Basic Biology Researchers: Study protein evolution and sequence-function relationships.

Use Cases

Protein Engineering Optimization:

Predict the impact of key residue substitutions on stability and function.

Screen optimal mutation combinations to enhance protein performance.

Drug Development:

Predict drug-resistance mutations in target proteins.

Evaluate stabilizing mutations for therapeutic protein products.

Inputs

Input (Required): Protein sequence composed of the 20 standard amino acids.

Outputs

Output: CSV file containing fitness scores for every possible single-point substitution.




Steps


1. Choose Sequence Fitness Mutation Effect in Mocha, enter a protein sequence containing standard amino acids, check the sequence, and submit.
2. After success, preview or download the CSV from the results panel. Use Display Score Heatmap to inspect scores by position and substitution, and compare candidates with the raw table.

5. Evolutionary Mutation Effect



Overview




Uses a Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) fitness model to evaluate all potential mutations across a protein sequence, calculating mutation scores to identify viable substitutions. It assesses the impact of specific amino acid changes, optimizes protein engineering workflows, and uncovers sequence variability and evolutionary constraints.

Target Users

Enzyme Designers: Use mutation scores to optimize enzymes for higher catalytic activity, specificity, and stability in industrial or biomedical applications.

Biologics Designers: Optimize antibodies, fusion proteins, and other biologics by identifying mutations that improve binding affinity, reduce immunogenicity, or improve pharmacokinetics.

Protein Researchers: Systematically evaluate mutations to accelerate sequence-structure-function investigations for de novo design or experimental hypothesis validation.

Use Cases

Mutation Scoring and Analysis: Scores all possible substitutions across a protein sequence. By substituting each amino acid position with all alternate amino acids, the MSA-based model calculates log-probability differences to help identify promising candidate mutations.

Inputs

Input (Required): Protein sequence composed of the 20 standard amino acids.

Outputs

Chain ID (Required): Identifier of the chain to undergo mutation scanning (e.g., Chain A).

Outputs

Mutation scan results file (CSV format) containing each mutation site, substitution type, and corresponding ΔΔGvalue (in kcal/mol). Lower ΔΔG indicates improved binding affinity after mutation (negative values indicate enhanced binding; positive values indicate weakened binding).




Steps


1. Import a complex containing the interacting chains, choose Binding Affinity Mutation Scoring in Mocha, and specify chains as required by the form. This example uses public 1BRS imported as a sanitized CIF, with chain parameter A,D.
2. After success, open the results panel to inspect and download the MutXaff CSV. Check each mutation position, substitution, score field, and unit.
